propositions: Bridge orchestration logic must be extracted into a runner-neutral packaged Python core exposed through three public interfaces: Python library (rebar.bridge_run), CLI (rebar bridge run --profile), and MCP (write-gated bridge_run tool), available from pip, Homebrew wheel-backed, and MCP Registry/uvx installs.

Five execution profiles (reconcile-check, dry-run, bootstrap-strict, bootstrap-throttle, live) must map to corresponding legacy CLI invocations while preserving existing behavior for direct callers; the new public operation uses canonical noun 'profile' but provider configuration retains 'MODE' environment variable compatibility.

Provider workflows (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab) must invoke exactly 'rebar bridge run' as an installed CLI entrypoint with no repository-local runner script, while existing checked-out workflows calling 'rebar reconcile --mode' retain their defaults and benign results (3/4/75).

The runner must validate environments, enforce 3600-second timeout, validate pause markers, translate legacy benign results to canonical success, and deliver strict ticket-store outcomes with run id, bot identity, and REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always; delivery failure returns exit code 1 with diagnostics.

Provider wrapper schemas and embedded shell must be validated offline: GitLab schema uses vendored immutable Draft-07 with verified SHA-256 provenance, and all shell is linted with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0; missing or mismatched tooling fails validation.

The wheel must pass content validation and prove availability across all supported install shapes (pip, Homebrew wheel-backed, MCP Registry/uvx) outside the repository, with explicit repo_root parameter overriding inherited REBAR_ROOT.
